title: Unified Inference: Product overview, PRD, roadmap, pricing, and release notes
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

Redwood's Unified Inference product provides a single developer experience and operational surface for running LLM inference across Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments. This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, design constraints, roadmap themes for the next 12 months, pricing and packaging guidance, and the release notes for the current major release (v3.2).

Goals and success metrics

- Primary goals:
  - Make inference predictable and economical for engineering teams by providing a unified API and automated performance controls.
  - Enable enterprise readiness (SLA, compliance, private deployments) without duplicating engineering efforts across deployment modes.
  - Reduce unit inference cost through batching, caching, and model-routing recommendations.
- Success metrics (12-month targets):
  - Reduce median per-token cost for our top 30 customers by 18% (QoQ).
  - 99.95% platform availability for Hosted API; Dedicated customers: 99.9% SLA.
  - Increase adoption of Redwood Optimize recommendations to 40% of active accounts.

Audience and scope

- Primary audience: product managers, engineering managers, SREs, solutions engineers, and sales engineering.
- Scope: covers product requirements and implementation details for Unified Inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes; does not include SDK reference or low-level runtime kernel docs (see eng-serving-runtime).

1) Product requirements (PRD)

1.1 Core capabilities (MUST)

- Unified REST/SDK API for: text generation, chat (stateful), embeddings, and reranking.
- Model catalog with: model metadata (architecture, quantization profile, latency/cost profile), compatible model variants, and version pinning.
- Smart routing policy engine: route by latency, cost, region, customer tier, or custom policies.
- Prefix/KV caching and automatic batching with configurable SLOs per route.
- Observability: per-request tracing, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards.
- Deployment parity: identical API surface and rollout semantics (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

1.2 Secondary capabilities (SHOULD)

- Automatic model quantization recommendation engine (profiles tested in quantization-profiles).
- Reranking pipelines with integrated eval hooks and quality regression alerts.
- Built-in rate limiting and quotas per API key/route.

1.3 Constraints and non-goals (WON'T)

- We will not ship first-party large model training capabilities as part of Unified Inference (out of scope).
- No custom model training within the hosted offering in this phase. Private customers can bring models via onprem packaging but training tooling is separate.

1.4 Success criteria for GA

- API parity completed and documented with SDK examples for Node/Python/Go.
- Automated rollout patterns (canary & automatic fallback) tested with >5 production customers.
- Latency SLOs validated: median p95 latency for text-generation < 220ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on standard catalog models for Hosted.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency reports available in Console for all customers.

2) Design and architecture highlights

2.1 High-level architecture

- Control plane (Redwood Console and API): stores model catalog, routing policies, rollout configs, and customer metadata.
- Serving runtime (compute plane): GPU-optimized inference engine with continuous batching, KV cache management, and quantization-friendly execution.
- Smart router: policy engine that selects target model variant and deployment zone based on route policy and real-time capacity signals.
- Caching layer: prefix cache + shared KV shards for common contexts.
- Observability pipeline: request tracing -> ingest -> per-route dashboards and alerts.

2.2 API contract (excerpt)

- POST /v1/generate
  - body: {"model":"redwood-unified-3.2","input":"...","route":"customer:chat-default","max_tokens":256,"stream":true}
  - response: streaming tokens with metadata for token_cost_usd and token_latency_ms

- POST /v1/embeddings
  - body: {"model":"embed-compact-1","inputs":["...","..."]}
  - response: {"data":[{"embedding":[...],"index":0}, ...], "usage":{"tokens":...}}

2.3 Routing and fallback policies

- Policy precedence: explicit route policy > customer tier policy > global defaults.
- Fallbacks: when a target model variant is unavailable, router attempts (in order): same-architecture quantized variant -> lower-capacity region -> compatible open model.
- Throttling/Load Shedding: if latency SLO endangered, router triggers degraded mode: enable smaller model variants + reduced max_tokens.

2.4 Observability and quality guardrails

- Console will surface: per-route token cost, median/p95 latency, error rates, cache hit ratio, and model-specific quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/regression test pass rate where applicable).
- Quality regression pipeline ties to prompt-sets-and-benchmarks and runs nightly for production-critical flows. Alerts created when regression exceeds configured thresholds.

3) Roadmap & themes (next 12 months)

Topline themes:
- Cost Controls and Model Economics (Q4 2026–Q1 2027): improve recommendations, autoscaling policies sensitive to unit-cost signals, and per-request cost profiling.
- Enterprise and Compliance (Q1–Q2 2027): expand Private deployment automation, KMS/HSM integrations, and SOC2/ISO evidence packs.
- Performance and Reliability (continuous): runtime kernel optimizations, KV cache sharding, and accelerated fallbacks.
- Developer Experience (Q2–Q3 2027): better SDKs, in-console quickstarts, and pre-built rollout templates.

Milestones (high-level):
- 2026-11: v3.2 GA (current release) — unified API parity, basic routing & fallback, Console token-level reports.
- 2027-02: Redwood Optimize v2 integration — automated batching/quantization suggestions in Console.
- 2027-05: Private Deployment Quickstart v1 — automated VPC onboarding & KMS integration.
- 2027-08: Dedicated Autoscaling policies GA — predictable burst capacity and long-running reservations visibility.
- 2027-11: Quality-first Rollouts — canary evaluation using prompt-set regressions and automatic rollback on quality drops.

4) Pricing and packaging notes

Principles:
- Pricing should reflect unit economics (per-token inference compute + model complexity adjustment) while remaining predictable for customers.
- Offer clear upgrade paths from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.

4.1 Hosted (public API)

- Base tiers:
  - Developer (freemium up to $50/mo usage credits).
  - Growth: $0.0009 / token for standard generation models; $0.0025 / token for high-quality models; embeddings $0.0007 / embedding request unit (50 tokens eq).
  - Enterprise: custom pricing with volume discounts and committed spend credits.
- Add-ons: higher retention for observability, premium SLA, extended eval support.

4.2 Dedicated (reserved capacity)

- Pricing components: monthly reservation (per-GPU-equivalent), usage overage per token (reduced rate), and optional premium support.
- Example: 8x A100-equivalent pool reserved = $95k/mo baseline (illustrative), overage billed at 50% of hosted per-token rate.

4.3 Private (VPC / on-prem)

- One-time platform licensing + annual support and maintenance.
- Additional engineering engagement for onprem packaging, security hardening, and compliance evidence.

4.4 Packaging guidance for Sales Engineers

- Small production teams: start with Growth Hosted, enable Redwood Optimize suggestions, and instrument cost dashboards.
- High-volume or regulated customers: propose Dedicated with a 6–12 month reservation and Private for air-gapped requirements.
- Always recommend a 30–60 day pilot with usage baseline and a follow-up review to size Dedicated reservations.

5) Release notes (v3.2) — 2026-11-24

Highlights:
- Unified API parity: single /v1 API for generation, chat, embeddings with SDK support for Node/Python/Go.
- Smart routing: initial policy engine with latency- and cost-based routing and fallback to quantized variants.
- Console: token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and rollout controls (canary + manual promotion).
- Observability: request tracing and integration points for external tracing systems (Jaeger/OTel).
- Performance: runtime improvements yielding 12% lower median latency on standard catalog models.

Migration notes and breaking changes:
- API change: embedding responses now include explicit "usage.tokens" field; clients should update SDKs if using raw responses. SDKs updated in 3.2 releases; recommend upgrading within 30 days.
- Model naming: model IDs standardized to the pattern <family>-<quality>-<version> (e.g., redwood-unified-3.2). Existing aliases continue for 90 days; migration tooling available in Console.

Known issues (v3.2):
- Rare cache invalidation race causing elevated latency for large concurrent warm-up traffic (incidence <0.1%). Runbook created in eng-serving-runtime/runbooks.
- Private quickstart scripts require updated IAM role templates for certain cloud provider accounts. Customer success playbook updated.

6) Rollout & migration plan

- Staged rollout: internal alpha -> beta customers (10 customers) -> gradual GA (50% traffic week 1, 100% week 3).
- Migration checklist for customers:
  1. Run SDK compatibility check (scripts in eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates).
  2. Run a 7–14 day pilot to collect traffic profiles and cost baseline.
  3. If moving to Dedicated, size reservation based on pilot 95th percentile RPS and token usage.
  4. Enable canary rollout and monitor prompt-set regression tests.

Appendices

A. Example CLI quickstart

```bash
# generate with streaming
curl -s -N -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-unified-3.2","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":120,"stream":true}'
```
